lessons: A test written against an assumption only ever confirms the assumption. Bit us TWICE: a mock that answered any query let a malformed GraphQL query ship, and an allowlist test using an invented error message hid the fact every real message was redacted for two rounds. Use a shape the API actually sent.
Never redact the error that names the fix. The allowlist ate 'Did you mean to use an inline fragment on ConcreteRestSummaryData?' -- the exact sentence that solved the bug.
Redaction must not eat the answer either: blanking 'positions' and 'nextLocationUpdateExpectedBy' destroyed the shapes the probe existed to learn, one comment after warning about that exact mistake.
An arbitrary JSON blob from an external API grows without warning. device.info leaked IMEI/ICCID/SSID/cell-id into a file whose purpose is being pasted into chats.
Only real data can catch a semantic bug: 'Last night' was correctly formatted, honestly labelled, and wrong -- it read the in-progress window and would have shown 0 h.
Read the reference implementation before interrogating an API blindly. pytryfi's const.py had the answer to the sleep bug the whole time.
Judge sources by whether they were ever run. pytryfi has real users; the Hubitat driver was AI-generated by someone who said they had no collar.

Windows: pytest's temp dir can be blocked (PYTEST_ADDOPTS --basetemp); a USB camera belongs to one program at a time (Windows Settings > Camera counts); PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content mangles non-ASCII, so keep generated files ASCII.

dont_retry: Do not use the Hubitat/DeepSeek Fi driver code -- it is hallucinated and contradicts the real API on the root field, the auth model and every query shape
Do not read the newest daily rest window as 'last night' -- it is today, in progress, with SLEEP=0
Do not select sleepAmounts directly on RestSummary.data -- it is abstract, the inline fragment is required
Do not add a bare 'state' rule to the redactor -- it blanks lastConnectionState and destroys the charge/signal fields
Do not surface timeToEmptyS as 'days left' -- it swings 4 days to 12 hours with GPS
Do not run `kona cameras` and assume the camera works -- it only proves the device opens, not that frames arrive; use `kona camera-test`
I claimed walk detection required an owner's phone to be present. That was wrong -- the 2b probe detected a walk with no phone nearby. Escape and walk are independent.
